efficacy.note: ATM-low gastric cancer cell line NUGC4 was the most olaparib-sensitive; ATM proposed as a predictive biomarker, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: Our results demonstrate that ATM is a potential predictive biomarker for PARP-1 inhibitor activity in gastric cancer harboring disruption of p53, and that combined inhibition of ATM and PARP-1 is a rational strategy
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The same hypothesis was already in AstraZeneca's Study 39 registry record (NCT01063517, first posted 2010-02-05, ATM-negative PFS co-primary), so the model was in use before this first public paper.

efficacy.note: Primary PFS missed overall (HR 0.80) and in ATM-low (HR 0.74); OS, a secondary, improved (HR 0.56; ATM-low 0.35).
efficacy.quote: Olaparib/paclitaxel did not lead to a significant improvement in PFS versus placebo/paclitaxel (overall population: hazard ratio [HR], 0.80; median PFS, 3.91 v 3.55 months, respectively; ATMlow population: HR, 0.74; median PFS, 5.29 v 3.68 months, respectively).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (JCO paywalled). The abstract itself states the cell-line rationale and the ATM-predictiveness test, so the comparison is stated.
efficacy.judgement: Primary endpoint governs under v3: PFS was pre-specified primary (registry co-primaries: overall and ATM-negative PFS) and missed in both populations, so contra even though OS, a secondary, was significant and larger in ATM-low. The source reads the OS result as supporting the hypothesis, recorded as source_calls_it partial. The trial combined olaparib with paclitaxel at 100 mg BID whereas the model tested olaparib alone.

efficacy.note: Phase 3 OS missed in both co-primary populations: overall HR 0.79 (p=0.026 vs 0.025 bar) and ATM-negative HR 0.73 (p=0.25).
efficacy.quote: The GOLD study did not meet its primary objective of showing a significant improvement in overall survival with olaparib in the overall or ATM-negative population of Asian patients with advanced gastric cancer.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Lancet Oncol paywalled); the abstract carries the primary result for both populations. Registry results posted 2018-11-07, after the 2017 epub.
efficacy.judgement: The model's patient-level call (ATM loss picks responders) is the one contradicted: the ATM-negative HR (0.73, p=0.25) was no better than the overall HR (0.79), which itself narrowly missed its 0.025 bar. The track stays contra; the overall near-miss is recorded in the note, not scored. Paired comparison: GOLD cites only the phase 2, not the cell-line paper.

efficacy.model: Cross-indication inference: PARP-inhibitor activity in HR-deficient tumours applied to platinum-responsive gastric cancer (pamiparib)
efficacy.note: Pamiparib maintenance after platinum response missed PFS (HR 0.8, p=0.14); OS numerically favoured placebo.
efficacy.quote: Maintenance pamiparib did not meet statistical significance for superiority versus placebo for PFS, but was well tolerated with few treatment discontinuations; no unexpected safety signals were identified.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (open access, not read in full). No gastric-specific preclinical model for pamiparib was found; the trial paper's rationale is PARPi approvals in other tumours plus HR-pathway mutation frequency in gastric cancer.
efficacy.reason: HRD inference failed in gastric maintenance
efficacy.judgement: Second member drug, separate track: pamiparib went into gastric cancer on other indications' PARPi data and the frequency of HR-gene mutations, not on a gastric disease model, so this is a cross_indication track rather than part of the cell-line track. Scored contra at class level because the primary endpoint (investigator PFS) missed. A reviewer who prefers to keep cross-indication inferences out of the figure can drop this entry; the olaparib track is unaffected.

efficacy.population: Metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after >=1 line, unselected, stratified by 17-gene HRD status (NCI10066, n=51)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC10844282). Registry NCT03008278 results first posted 2025-06-04 (ORR, PFS); the paper (epub 2023-12-22) is the earlier public comparison. The go-rule sentence: 'The therapy would be worthy of further investigation if there were >=1 response in tumours with HRD alterations and >=4 responses in tumours without evidence of HRD alterations'. No rucaparib or pamiparib patient data on this track.
efficacy.quote: For the six patients with PRs, two had HRD-positive tumours, one HRD-negative cancer, and three did not have genomic results.
efficacy.note: Phase 2 go-rule needed >=4 responses in HRD-negative tumours; one seen (ORR 6/43, 14%, CI 4.7-25.6 spans the 5% null).
efficacy.short: Hypoxia-sensitisation bar missed in HRD-negative gastric
efficacy.judgement: The paper states the comparison itself ('Our preclinical work revealed tumour hypoxia induces HRD... We aimed to induce tumour hypoxia with ramucirumab thereby sensitising tumours to olaparib'). The hypoxia mechanism is tested in HR-proficient tumours, where the pre-specified rule required >=4 responses and one occurred; the overall ORR CI includes the <=5% null. The authors call the regimen active versus historical ramucirumab (14% vs 3%), so source_calls_it is partial and the status is contra on the primary endpoint rule, not same. Single-arm phase 1/2 with three responders unsequenced, hence medium confidence. Dose and engagement unchanged.

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11592444; brief report, epub 2024-10-29). Described as a multicentre retrospective observational cancer-gene-panel study yet the olaparib arm is called randomised; arm counts (76 + 65) do not match the stated total of 132; no registry record found, so registry_date is null. Does not cite the PDX paper. Rucaparib and pamiparib have no patient data in this genotype.
efficacy.quote: Results showed that the olaparib plus paclitaxel group had a significantly longer overall survival (OS) than the paclitaxel alone group.
efficacy.note: HR-gene-PV gastric cancer (germline BRCA1/2 enriched to 50%): OS HR 0.57 with olaparib + paclitaxel, 0.36 in the HRD-positive subset.
efficacy.short: HR-mutant gastric patients benefit from olaparib
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison I made: the PDX model (model_src) predicted PARPi benefit confined to BRCA2-driven gastric cancers; this Kyoto series reports longer OS with olaparib plus paclitaxel in HR-gene-mutant gastric cancer, direction only. The population (pathogenic variants in any of 10 HR genes) is broader than the model's BRCA2-plus-LOH genotype, and the report is internally inconsistent, so confidence is low; a later genotype-exact case strengthens it (next entry).

efficacy.judgement: Strengthens, not a status change: one case report (n=1, selection-biased by publication) whose genotype matches the PDX model's responder definition exactly (germline BRCA2 loss-of-function plus loss of the wild-type allele). Paired by me; the case report does not cite the PDX paper.

safety.model: Rat and dog general toxicology, up to 26 weeks (olaparib)
safety.note: Rat/dog hematopoietic toxicity matched anemia and neutropenia in olaparib patients; the FDA comparison is in ovarian/mixed tumours, imported.
safety.short: Marrow toxicity predicted, seen in patients
safety.quote: In general toxicology studies, the major target organ of toxicity was the hematopoietic system, which is consistent with adverse reactions reported in patients treated with olaparib.
safety.confidence_note: Read from the bundled review text (sources/206162/206162Orig1s000PharmR.txt). The patient side of the FDA statement is the olaparib clinical programme at the 2014 ovarian approval, not gastric patients.
safety.judgement: On-target class harm, so it pools across indications; imported from ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170) because the regulator's stated comparison was made there. Magnitude is direction only: cytopenias appeared in rats and dogs at 2-4% of clinical exposure, so the animals over-predicted sensitivity while the harm itself held. model_first_use_year is null: the review does not date the studies.
safety.magnitude_basis: harm present in both; animal cytopenias at 2-4% of clinical exposure

safety.model: Rat and dog general toxicology, up to 26 weeks (olaparib)
safety.note: In gastric patients, grade 3+ neutropenia 30% vs 23% and leucopenia 16% vs 10% with placebo: the predicted marrow harm held with paclitaxel.
safety.short: Neutropenia excess seen in gastric patients
safety.quote: In the overall patient population, the most common grade 3 or worse adverse events in the olaparib plus paclitaxel group were neutropenia (78 [30%] of 262 patients), leucopenia (42 [16%]), and decreased neutrophil count (40 [15%])
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the excess over placebo plus paclitaxel (30% vs 23% neutropenia) is modest and paclitaxel itself causes neutropenia, so attribution to olaparib rests on the arm difference.
safety.judgement: Paired comparison: GOLD does not cite the toxicology; the model side is the FDA review. Scored same (not other) because this is the on-target harm the species predicted for this product. No unpredicted harm the species could have shown appeared: the two treatment-related deaths (liver injury, cardiac failure) were one per arm.
safety.magnitude_basis: harm present; 7-point excess in grade 3+ neutropenia over placebo plus paclitaxel
